extracted.intended_audience: State Apprenticeship Agencies (SAAs), Registration Agencies, program sponsors/employers, Department of Labor staff, and stakeholders responding to the proposed 29 CFR parts 29 and 30 rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluate, implement, or comment on the Department of Labor's proposed regulatory requirements (29 CFR parts 29 and 30) for recognition/derecognition of SAAs, program registration, program reviews, complaints, data reporting, and related procedural and substantive standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: State apprentice record reporting system requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: State system capable of reporting individual apprentice record level information to the Department in a manner that meets requirements prescribed by the Administrator and minimum security requirements consistent with FERPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System would be a vital component to ensure nationally consistent data reporting. Department is not mandating RAPIDS but expects consistent-format reporting; some States may use RAPIDS or other case management systems and upload results into RAPIDS quarterly. SAAs may retain their own systems but must report in a consistent format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent reporting format requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: States/SAAs must report apprenticeship data to OA in a consistent format even if they maintain their own internal systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposal does not require abandonment of State systems but would require reporting in a consistent format to ensure national consistency across State lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of denial and derecognition procedures (§29.29)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.29 would consolidate processes and procedures concerning denial of State Apprenticeship Plans and derecognition of existing SAAs into one section, updating language and aligning with the State apprenticeship planning process in §29.27.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures for hearings after final determinations largely same as current regulation but aligned with deregistration hearing procedures in proposed §29.21; State obligations after derecognition largely retain current language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written notice content for denial/derecognition (§29.29(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: When OA denies a State Apprenticeship Plan or derecognizes an SAA, OA must provide a written notice to the State that includes the reason(s) for the denial/derecognition, the remedial measures the State must take, and a timeline for addressing those measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeline must be no longer than 12 months after the written notice date; corrective action plans required for provisionally recognized SAAs but not for derecognition (instead, timeline to complete remedial measures). The 12-month cap is intended to permit changes including State law changes while ensuring urgency.

rubrics_metrics.name: 12-month remedial timeline cap
rubrics_metrics.description: A State shall be given no longer than 12 months after the date of the written notice to address identified remedial measures leading to denial or derecognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department determined 12 months appropriate to allow potential changes to State laws yet to avoid an open-ended remediation period; time needed may vary by facts but cap ensures expeditious resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator's final determination and hearing opportunity (§29.29(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a State does not remedy the reasons for denial/derecognition within the identified timeframe, the Administrator may issue a final determination that includes the reason(s), and the State may request a hearing within 30 calendar days of the final determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department will provide public notice if a State has been derecognized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing request transmission and administrative file provision (§29.29(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A State's request for a hearing must be sent to the OALJ and the Administrator, who transmits the request to the Office of the Solicitor. The Administrator must promptly provide the OALJ with the administrative file containing all relevant documents relied upon in making the final determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows existing procedural requirements; aligns hearing process with administrative adjudicatory procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment of hearing procedures with deregistration hearings (§29.29(a)(4)–(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §§29.29(a)(4) and (5) update existing provisions to align the denial/derecognition hearing procedures with the deregistration hearing procedures described in proposed §29.21.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive procedural elements are updated to be consistent across sections governing deregistration and derecognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary withdrawal/derecognition procedures (§29.26(a)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures applicable when an SAA voluntarily seeks withdrawal from recognition are described, recognizing States' discretion to relinquish recognition of recognized SAAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges voluntary actions by States and provides corresponding procedural framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to sponsors after derecognition and sponsor application window (§29.29(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrator must notify sponsors in the State where the SAA is derecognized that the Department will cease to recognize their previously registered programs unless the sponsor submits an application for registration with OA within 45 calendar days after the final agency determination to derecognize the SAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsor applications would be reviewed per proposed §29.10; OA would review applications within 90 calendar days and approve if they meet §29.10(a)/(b); applications not meeting requirements would be denied and §29.10(c) procedures apply to declined applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: OA review timeline for sponsor registration applications (90 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 90 calendar days of receiving a sponsor's application for registration after derecognition, OA would review the application to determine if it meets registration requirements described in §29.10(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approvals follow §29.10(b) procedures; denials follow §29.10(c) procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: State obligations after derecognition—records transfer (§29.29(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: When an SAA is denied recognition, derecognized, or voluntarily withdraws, the State must transfer apprenticeship-related records and information to the Department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures continuity of operations and Department's ability to fulfill obligations to apprentices and sponsors.

rubrics_metrics.name: State must notify sponsors about loss of federal registration (§29.29(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: State must notify sponsors that their programs will no longer be registered for Federal purposes as of 45 calendar days after the Administrator's final determination; sponsors interested in registration must submit an application to OA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification aligns with paragraph (b) sponsor application window and OA review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: State cooperation during transition (§29.29(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: States must cooperate fully with the Administrator during a transition period, maintaining open lines of communication and facilitating timely transfer of pertinent records and information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included to ensure smooth, seamless continuity in the National Apprenticeship System and to support Department obligations to apprentices and sponsors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of Participation and information sharing for other laws (§29.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.30 allows OA/SAAs to provide a Certificate of Participation and apprentice participation information required to document compliance with other Federal or State laws, provided such disclosure is consistent with applicable Federal/State privacy laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses needs where apprentice information is necessary for implementation of laws like Davis-Bacon, WIOA, IRA, or other Federal/State benefit programs; sharing permissible if consistent with privacy and other laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace part 30 cross-references to specific part 29 sections with 'part 29'
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical change: replace all cross-references in part 30 that cite specific sections of part 29 with citations that cite to 'part 29' to avoid outdated references after reorganization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affects multiple sections enumerated in part 30; intended to reduce need for future updates after further reorganizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology change: 'compliance review' → 'program review' in part 30
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace terms 'EEO compliance review' and 'compliance review' with 'program review' throughout part 30 to reflect scope of OA's reviews covering both parts 29 and 30 components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strictly a terminological change; not intended to alter the nature of reviews described in part 30.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'days' as calendar days (replace 'business days')
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed replacement of 'business days' with 'days' defined in 29 CFR 29.2 to mean calendar days, not business days or workdays; where sponsors had 30 business days it becomes 45 calendar days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change intended for consistency with part 29 and to improve clarity for the regulated community; viewed as roughly equivalent to previous business-day timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program reviews triggered by credible information of noncompliance (§30.13 and part 29 alignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Program reviews must be conducted if the Registration Agency receives credible information or allegations that a program is not being operated in accordance with program standards and requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program reviews increase worker protections and program transparency by ensuring compliance and identifying deficiencies requiring remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect complainant identity when practicable (§30.14(c)(1)(vi))
rubrics_metrics.description: Add requirement that the Registration Agency protect the identity of the complainant to the extent practicable when processing complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintains consistency with complaint protections proposed under part 29; intended to enable apprentices to file complaints without fear of retaliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension step prior to deregistration (§30.15 and §29.20 deregisration changes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Add an intermediary suspension step that allows a Registration Agency to suspend registration of new apprentices while a sponsor implements a voluntary compliance action plan or until a final order is issued in deregistration proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removes prior requirement that proceedings be instituted within 45 days or suspension be lifted; allows suspension for a set period to resolve deficiencies and avoid immediate deregistration and subsequent reregistration burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability provision addition to part 30
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a severability provision in part 30 identical to that proposed in 29 CFR 29.5 to maintain consistency between the two parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical/conforming edit to ensure legal drafting consistency across parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on non-disclosure and non-compete provisions in apprenticeship agreements (§29.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed prohibitions on non-compete and certain non-disclosure provisions in apprenticeship agreements to prevent anticompetitive restraints on apprentices during the term of apprenticeship programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department acknowledges potential disincentive to employer training investment but finds macroeconomic benefits (increased competition, apprentice mobility, wage gains, entrepreneurial opportunities) outweigh costs. Rationale and empirical citations provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation and use of National Occupational/Program Standards and Guidelines (§§29.13–29.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define and facilitate use of 'National Program Standards for Apprenticeship,' 'National Guidelines for Apprenticeship Standards,' and 'National Occupational Standards for Apprenticeship' to promote industry-recognized, standardized products that streamline registration and local adoption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These products provide templates, industry-validated training standards and curricula, and help sponsors/SAAs leverage national frameworks to expedite new occupation determinations and reduce time and cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic/regulatory significance criteria (E.O. 12866 and E.O. 13563 applicability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under E.O. 12866 and related guidance, a regulatory action is 'significant' if it meets criteria such as having an annual effect on the economy of $200 million or more, materially altering budgets/rights, creating interagency inconsistencies, or raising legal/policy issues needing centralized review. E.O. 13563 requires a reasoned determination that benefits justify costs, tailoring to least burden, and selection of approaches that maximize net benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department considers the proposed rule a significant regulatory action under E.O. 12866 and applies E.O. 13563 principles in its regulatory analysis (qualitative and quantitative cost/benefit discussion over a 10-year period, discounting at 3% and 7%).
